h: Plan your visit to Strangford Lough
p: How long should you give it? A couple of hours is a good guide for the aquarium and seal sanctuary, with time for a bite to eat. That leaves plenty of the day to explore the lough and the Ards Peninsula, which is a real treat if you've never been.

Strangford Lough itself is one of the great natural treasures of Northern Ireland. Its waters are protected for their rich marine life, and the shoreline is a magnet for birds, especially in the colder months when huge flocks of wildfowl arrive. Bring binoculars if you have them, and keep an eye out for seals in the water; spotting a wild one after visiting the sanctuary is a lovely moment.

Tips for your visit: check the talk times when you arrive so you can catch the feeds and keeper chats. Pack a waterproof for walking around the village, as the weather off the lough can change in no time. If you're planning to cross on the ferry, give yourself a bit of flexibility, as queues can build at busy times.

Over the water at Strangford, the National Trust's Castle Ward is a fascinating house and estate, and fans of Game of Thrones may recognise parts of it from filming. Back on the peninsula, Mount Stewart near Greyabbey has famous gardens that are a joy to wander, and the ruins of Grey Abbey are worth a stop too.
In Portaferry itself, the old tower house of Portaferry Castle stands close to the waterfront, and the village has pubs and cafés for a relaxed end to the day with a view across the water.
